paper.title_en: Hydrostatic Equilibrium Estimate of the Fuzzy Dark Matter Mass from Dwarf Spheroidals: Method and Systematics
paper.abstract_en: We present an estimator of an effective fuzzy (wave) dark matter (FDM) boson mass based on local hydrostatic equilibrium, which requires no soliton or other parametric density template. The condition requires the classical gravitational acceleration to be balanced by the gradient of the quantum potential in the Schrödinger--Poisson--Madelung system. We apply it to the density and enclosed-mass posteriors of nine Milky Way dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxies obtained with \textsc{pyGravSphere}. For each posterior realization, we determine by least squares the boson mass that best satisfies the force-balance condition over a fixed radial window. This gives a distribution of \(m_{21}\equiv m/10^{-21}\,\mathrm{eV}\) for each galaxy. The per-galaxy median masses range from \(m_{21}\sim 8\) to \(46\), corresponding to \(m\sim(0.8\text{--}4.6)\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{eV}\); Draco and Ursa Minor have the lowest median masses, while Carina and Sextans have the highest. The inverse-variance-weighted effective equilibrium mass of the nine galaxies is \(m=(1.31\pm0.35)\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{eV}\), with Draco and Ursa Minor contributing most of the weight. We also examine the systematic uncertainties in our results.
